meta.description: Assign cells to their sample of origin from cell or nucleus hashing (CITE-seq HTOs, MULTI-seq lipid/cholesterol tags, CellPlex CMOs) and call cross-sample doublets using Seurat HTODemux/MULTIseqDemux, hashsolo, demuxEM, GMM-Demux, and demuxmix. Use when assigning pooled hashed cells back to their sample, calling cross-sample doublets from HTO counts, choosing a demultiplexing method, deciding between hashtag and genetic demultiplexing, or rescuing an oversized Negative pile from weak HTO staining or ambient spillover.
meta.note: RE-AUDIT of a fixed Skill. Fresh independent auditor; different from both the 2026-09-19 original auditor (score 78) and the 2026-09-19 fixer (branch fix/sc-hashing, commit 0de5e440). Pre-fix report archived to F:\OpenScience\audits\_pre-fix-20260919\bio-single-cell-hashing-demultiplexing\. All 5 inputs below use freshly generated synthetic data (different seeds, different cell counts) from both the original auditor's and the fixer's own test data, to avoid re-measuring only the exact scenario the fixer was told about. Inputs unaffected by the fix diff (HTODemux canonical, modality-choice consultation, unequal-pooling stress) were not re-executed this round -- the diff (single-cell/hashing-demultiplexing/{SKILL.md,usage-guide.md,examples/hashsolo_scanpy.py} only) confirms those code paths are byte-identical to the same-day original audit that scored them 90, 88, and 92; those scores are not carried into this report's dynamic_score to avoid claiming an execution that did not happen this round.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated DOIs/PMIDs, p-values, sample sizes, or clinical claims in any of the 5 outputs; all reported numbers trace to code I executed this round or synthetic ground truth I generated.

practice_boundaries.detail: Skill remains scoped to lab computational sample-assignment, not patient diagnosis or treatment; no diagnostic/prescriptive language; a medical disclaimer is not applicable to this scope.

methodological_ground.detail: hashsolo's number_of_noise_barcodes fix, demuxmix's model='naive' fallback (with its accuracy trade-off honestly caveated and the convergence warning surfaced), and GMM-Demux's Gaussian-mixture approach all match verified tool behavior and documented statistics; no fallacy found.

code_usability.detail: All code I executed this round (fixed hashsolo pattern, fixed demuxmix tryCatch guard, GMM-Demux CLI pattern) ran to completion without syntax errors or missing dependencies on fresh, independently-generated data.

functional_suitability.note: All 5 named tools now have coverage: HTODemux/MULTIseqDemux (unchanged), hashsolo (P0 fixed), demuxmix (P1 crash-guard added), GMM-Demux (new, verified example), and demuxEM/pegasus (honestly documented as non-buildable on Windows rather than shipping an unverified example -- verified independently, see M4/recommendations). key_strengths: The P0 (hashsolo silently misclassifying 100% of cells Negative at 2 hashtags) is genuinely fixed: independently reproduced the original failure on fresh, unseen data (11.3% accuracy) and confirmed the fix recovers it (91.9% global, 100% singlet sample-ID agreement), deterministically.

The demuxmix P1 crash-guard fix is genuinely resolved, and the fixer's specific claim that manual clusterInit alone does NOT fix this crash (only model='naive' does) was independently verified true -- a checkable claim that held up.
The new GMM-Demux example is verified end-to-end on independently-generated data (1000/1000 global, 840/840 singlet sample-ID agreement), closing the 'no runnable example for 2 of 5 named tools' P1.

demuxEM/pegasus's Windows build failure is a genuine platform incompatibility (independently reproduced the exact LNK2001/getline linker error), not a fixer shortcut for skipping an inconvenient example.
All three fixed code paths (hashsolo, demuxmix naive-fallback, GMM-Demux) are independently verified fully deterministic on repeated identical input.

recommendations.title: GMM-Demux's SSD-mtx writer does not 'always' fail as SKILL.md states
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md says the SSD-mtx writer step 'always attempts to write a same-sample-droplet mtx file after classification and that step throws ValueError... even on an otherwise-correct run.' On a fresh 1000-cell 4-tag run, GMM-Demux exited 0 and wrote SSD_mtx/ without error.
recommendations.root_cause: The fixer's own test run happened to trigger the failure and generalized it as universal; it appears to be data- or environment-dependent rather than deterministic across all inputs.
recommendations.fix: Soften 'always attempts... and that step throws' to something like 'can throw... on some inputs/environments'; keep the underlying advice (judge success by GMM_full.csv, not exit code) unchanged, since it is safe regardless of whether the mtx step fails.

recommendations.title: No bundled example dataset for smoke-testing the fixed patterns
recommendations.problem: The Skill still ships no small synthetic HTO dataset alongside examples/, so verifying the hashsolo/demuxmix/GMM-Demux patterns requires generating data from scratch each time (as this audit and the original audit both did independently).
recommendations.root_cause: examples/ contains only code, no fixture data.
recommendations.fix: Add a small synthetic 2-3 tag HTO CSV under examples/data/ so the hashsolo and GMM-Demux patterns are runnable as-is without the agent first writing a data generator.
